Disclosure and suppression

Source: vignettes/articles/disclosure.Rmd
disclosure.Rmd

HCUP’s reporting rules prohibit reporting cells with 10 or fewer discharges and require that reported estimates represent at least two hospitals. Follow the terms of the applicable Data Use Agreement and institutional review. Suppression is a review aid, not a guarantee against every disclosure path.

Count data-frame cells

nis_cell_counts() counts unweighted discharges and distinct hospitals using year-scoped hospital IDs. This invented fixture has one cell with a small count and a separate cell with more than 10 discharges but support from only one hospital.

records <- data.frame(
  YEAR = rep(2020, 14),
  HOSP_NIS = c(1, 1, 2, rep(3, 11)),
  group = c(rep("A", 3), rep("B", 11)),
  estimate = c(rep(2.1, 3), rep(8.4, 11))
)
cell_estimates <- dplyr::summarise(
  dplyr::group_by(records, group),
  estimate = mean(estimate),
  .groups = "drop"
)
cells <- nis_cell_counts(records, by = "group") |>
  dplyr::left_join(cell_estimates, by = "group")
cells
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   group     n hospitals estimate
#>   <chr> <int>     <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 A         3         2      2.1
#> 2 B        11         1      8.4

A has three discharges across two hospitals; B has 11 discharges at one hospital. Counts are unweighted and the displayed estimate is only a made-up value.

Suppress data frames

For data frames, provide the count column and any estimate columns to mask. The default threshold is inclusive: counts at or below 10 are suppressed. Cells with fewer than two hospitals are marked as such.

nis_suppress(
  cells,
  count_col = "n",
  weighted_cols = "estimate",
  hospital_col = "hospitals"
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   group n            hospitals    estimate    
#>   <chr> <chr>        <chr>        <chr>       
#> 1 A     ≤10          ≤10          ≤10         
#> 2 B     <2 hospitals <2 hospitals <2 hospitals

The output suppresses A under the inclusive ≤10 discharge rule and marks B under the two-hospital rule, despite its count being above 10. When a table has totals or grouped subtotals, inspect them for complementary disclosure.

Suppress a gtsummary table

For a gtsummary::tbl_svysummary() object, nis_suppress() reads unweighted counts from the table’s cards, masks displayed statistics at or below the threshold, and marks the overall statistic in the same row. This route checks discharge counts only; it cannot check the two-hospital rule.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:

design <- nis_design(nis, heart_failure, keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, RACE))
#> Warning: Missing values are always removed in SQL aggregation functions.
#> Use `na.rm = TRUE` to silence this warning

#> Cohort: 54 discharges; weighted N 62.4; 9 hospitals across 1 years.
table_one <- gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
  design,
  by = RACE,
  include = c(AGE, FEMALE)
)
nis_suppress(table_one, threshold = 10)
#> `nis_suppress()` on a `tbl_svysummary` checks discharge counts only; it does

The masked table is a starting point for review. Use the data-frame route with nis_cell_counts() when both the discharge threshold and hospital count must be checked.

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • Suppressing only values below 10 misses the prohibited count of exactly 10; the default masks 10 and below.
  • A single-hospital cell needs review even when its discharge count is large.
  • Masking a cell can leave it derivable from totals, subtotals, or another table. Review the complete set of planned outputs.

See nis_cell_counts() and nis_suppress().
